audience: Students with basic programming knowledge learning assembly

progression.localImplementation: Native prose and public intermediate/final CLI checks; remote delivery and enforced instructor policies remain pending

title: Encode and decode QOI images
prerequisites: Unsigned byte extraction, bit fields and modulo arithmetic
Nested calls, full-width saved state and private arrays
Strict extents, image word layout and short file transfers
learningObjectives: Maintain a predictor and a 64-entry color cache
Decode all six QOI chunk types and reject malformed extents
Separate file RGBA bytes from stored color words and RGB display
Retain channels and colorspace as descriptive fields
Validate before publishing pixels or metadata
Produce equivalent legal encodings with uniform-image compression
Close descriptors on success, format errors, capacity errors and I/O failures

inputDomain.extent: One image, exact end marker and no trailing bytes
inputDomain.cache: 64 zero RGBA entries; RUN updates cache; no repeated adjacent INDEX slot
inputDomain.developmentStatus: 4 with zero count; outside completed interface contract

steps.title: Locate the first command before running it

quiz.prompt: What does the first bound call receive?

choices.text: The address of the first command.

hints.text: Separate the data fixture from the arguments of the selected caller mode.
Stop at bound_call and compare a0 with the dimensions control; source bytes remain independently inspectable.

steps.title: Separate the two packed dimensions

quiz.prompt: Which operation should recover the upper field?

choices.text: A word-sized left shift by thirty-two.
A logical sixty-four-bit right shift by thirty-two.

hints.text: Both fields are unsigned even though the host register API represents raw bits as a signed Long.
Use full-width shifts; isolate the low half without retaining any original high bits.

steps.title: Reject dimensions before multiplying them

quiz.prompt: Why must a high-bit dimension fail?

choices.text: Its unsigned value exceeds the local limit.
It describes a negative number of transparent pixels.
It is an alternative spelling of zero.

hints.text: Establish each field’s domain separately.
Test nonzero and unsigned less-than sixty-five before computing the product.

steps.title: Return a conservative byte bound

quiz.prompt: What does the returned sixty-two describe?

hints.text: Count fixed framing and per-pixel maximum separately.
Five times eight plus twenty-two is sixty-two; keep the result in a full-width register.

steps.title: Guard the byte count before a pointer access

quiz.prompt: Which input must be rejected without a header load?

choices.text: An unaligned byte pointer by itself.
A count with bit sixty-three set.
A valid RGB sample equal to zero.

hints.text: Bounds are about the unsigned count, not the signed appearance of a register value.
Compare against 20502 first, then against twenty-three, using the supplied error returns.

steps.title: Check every magic byte

quiz.prompt: Why use byte comparisons here?

choices.text: The file’s literal byte order stays explicit.
The magic has a signed numerical meaning.
A byte pointer must be four-byte aligned.

hints.text: The first four bytes are a literal signature.
Check 71, 6f, 69 and 66 in hexadecimal at offsets zero through three.

steps.title: Assemble and bound big-endian dimensions

quiz.prompt: What would a little-endian native load of 00 00 00 08 produce?

choices.text: The address of the first pixel.

hints.text: Byte order belongs to the file field, not to the simulator’s configured word storage.
Use unsigned loads and explicitly positioned shifts, then apply the dimension checks before multiplication.

steps.title: Validate flags and retain private metadata

quiz.prompt: Where should these accepted header fields go first?

choices.text: Into the first four framebuffer pixels.

hints.text: A valid header does not establish a valid command stream.
Use private frame offsets 88, 92, 96 and 100; defer caller stores until marker validation.

steps.title: Give each cursor and predictor its own state

quiz.prompt: Which initial value belongs to the previous pixel?

hints.text: The predictor and the cache have different initial conditions.
Set the predictor alpha to 255, retain a separate total, and derive the payload limit by reserving the final eight bytes.

steps.title: Clear all sixty-four cache entries

quiz.prompt: How many eight-byte stores clear the cache?

hints.text: Each entry occupies four bytes, and there are sixty-four entries.
Use a separate advancing pointer so the retained cache base does not move.

steps.title: Load one bounded tag

quiz.prompt: What proves that a tag byte is available?

choices.text: The remaining output capacity is nonzero.
The cursor is strictly before the payload end.

hints.text: The logical payload limit excludes all eight marker bytes.
Test remaining pixels first, then compare the full-width cursor with the payload end before loading.

steps.title: Dispatch full-byte tags before classes

quiz.prompt: What goes wrong if fe is first treated as class 11?

choices.text: It is mistaken for a run of sixty-three pixels.
It becomes a one-byte RGB command.

hints.text: Two full-byte tags occupy values that otherwise resemble the run class.
Compare the complete tag with 254 and 255, then shift the remaining tag right by six for its class.

steps.title: Decode a run and prove its output extent

quiz.prompt: Why add one to the stored field?

choices.text: Every run includes an extra marker pixel.
The field stores run length minus one.

hints.text: Legal run lengths are one through sixty-two.
Mask with 63, add one, then use an unsigned comparison with remaining pixels.

steps.title: Insert the reconstructed color into its cache slot

quiz.prompt: Which value belongs in the cache entry?

choices.text: RGB with alpha forced to zero.

hints.text: A slot identifies storage; it is not enough information to reconstruct the color.
Use weights 3, 5, 7 and 11, mask the sum to six bits and multiply the slot by four for its address.

steps.title: Make public stores conditional on publication mode

quiz.prompt: What should validation mode publish at this stage?

choices.text: A header word in the framebuffer.

hints.text: Reconstructing a private color does not authorize a caller store.
Use the supplied fp flag; route the disabled path through after_w_emit without touching s5.

steps.title: Advance one repeated output pixel at a time

quiz.prompt: Which cursor stays fixed during run expansion?

hints.text: The tag described all repetitions at once.
Reduce s2 and t3 for each pixel; return to the tag loop only when t3 reaches zero.

steps.title: Observe the first run before adding RGB

quiz.prompt: Why does slot fifty-three now differ from its initial value?

choices.text: The RGB handler has already changed it.
The first reconstructed run pixel was inserted.
Every cache entry was initialized opaque.

hints.text: Pause before the unfinished RGB body, after the run and the next tag load.
Compare the private cache word at slot 53 with the initial all-zero word; inspect its alpha byte too.

steps.title: Load RGB while retaining previous alpha

quiz.prompt: Where does this command obtain alpha?

hints.text: RGB contains only three new component bytes.
Reserve the marker, check three available bytes and retain the predictor’s high byte before packing.

steps.title: Pack four unsigned components into one color word

quiz.prompt: What is the packed red word with opaque alpha?

hints.text: The file supplied RGB order, but the numerical word has blue in its low byte.
Position the four independent eight-bit fields and combine them without sign-extending a partial word.

steps.title: Fetch an index and check adjacency

quiz.prompt: What does INDEX restore along with RGB?

choices.text: The preceding pixel’s alpha regardless of cache.

hints.text: The cache stores complete words, including invisible component differences.
Compare the tag’s slot with s6, load its four-byte entry with a consistent unsigned representation and retain that slot for adjacency.

steps.title: Apply three biased two-bit changes

quiz.prompt: What operation follows each component addition?

hints.text: QOI changes wrap; they do not clamp.
Extract fields at shifts 4,2 and 0, subtract the bias and mask the resulting components with 255.

steps.title: Combine green change with its residuals

quiz.prompt: What does the high nibble of 97 contribute?

hints.text: The two nibbles are residuals, not independent absolute changes.
Decode dG=5, dR-dG=1 and dB-dG=-1 before applying any channel addition.

steps.title: Replace all four components for RGBA

quiz.prompt: Which component is explicitly replaced here but retained by RGB?

hints.text: The full ff tag has four following component bytes.
Load the fourth byte into t7; do not reuse alpha from the preceding color.

steps.title: Inspect the completed private reconstruction

quiz.prompt: Does reconstructing eight pixels establish full file validity?

choices.text: No; marker and exact extent remain.
Yes; the remaining bytes are ignored.
Only when the last pixel is opaque.

hints.text: Pixel completion and stream completion are separate conditions.
Inspect s2, the two input pointers and the final alpha before allowing metadata publication.

steps.title: Require the exact eight-byte marker

quiz.prompt: Why reject a cursor short of the payload end?

choices.text: It necessarily identifies a smaller valid image.
Zero bytes automatically terminate QOI data.

hints.text: The declared pixel count must meet the framing boundary exactly.
Check cursor equality first, then seven zeros followed by one; do not consume marker bytes as samples.

steps.title: Publish metadata only after complete validation

quiz.prompt: Which result belongs in v1 for validation?

hints.text: The validator’s result unit differs from loader and decoder result units.
Copy four words only after the marker stage, then return the retained total rather than the now-zero remaining count.

steps.title: Repeat validation with a trailing byte

quiz.prompt: What should happen to metadata on this late error?

choices.text: It retains fields published before the marker.

hints.text: A late format error has the same metadata promise as an early one.
Use the separate trailer recipe and compare every descriptor byte with its pre-call value.

steps.title: Validate through a private decoder descriptor

quiz.prompt: Why pass a private metadata destination?

choices.text: The validator requires a global scratch object.
It changes the file’s channel count.
The decoder has no public metadata output argument.

hints.text: A nested call needs its own result object and preserved arguments.
Retain bytes/count/output/capacity in s0..s3 and use sp+80 as the descriptor destination.

steps.title: Compare capacity in pixels with unsigned arithmetic

quiz.prompt: Which unit belongs in this comparison?

hints.text: Use the validator’s pixel count directly.
Compare s3 with v1 unsigned; the supplied capacity return leaves the output unchanged.

steps.title: Run the accepted publishing pass

quiz.prompt: Which state must be reinitialized for the second pass?

hints.text: Validation completed an entire reconstruction already.
Restore the original source/count and pass s2 as the output pointer with t9=1; the shared entry establishes fresh per-invocation state.

steps.title: Return both decoder dimensions in full

quiz.prompt: What would truncating this result to a word lose?

hints.text: This result is a pair of dimensions, not a byte count.
Zero-extend width, shift height left by 32 and combine them before the full-width return.

steps.title: Inspect stored alpha separately from displayed RGB

quiz.prompt: Which observation proves that alpha was restored by the final INDEX?

choices.text: The final stored high byte isff.

hints.text: The display and the file preserve different observable information.
Read all four little-endian bytes of both words; do not infer alpha from RGB brightness.

steps.title: Validate the encoder descriptor before pixels

quiz.prompt: Which error takes priority over capacity?

hints.text: The descriptor defines what input pixels and output header would mean.
Validate widths/heights in 1..64, channels in 3..4 and colorspace in 0..1 before using pixel data.

steps.title: Preflight the conservative encoder capacity

quiz.prompt: Why can capacity thirty-five still be rejected for this image?

choices.text: A QOI stream must have a multiple-of-four length.
The encoder always writes sixty-two bytes.
The interface requires the conservative sixty-two-byte bound.

hints.text: Required capacity and returned length have different roles.
Calculate the bound from validated dimensions and use an unsigned full-width comparison before any pixel load.

steps.title: Retain encoder metadata and locate its private cache

quiz.prompt: Why retain header fields before the pixel loop?

choices.text: The cache itself stores the header.
Temporary calculations may overwrite their registers.
The file requires a new dimension for every pixel.

hints.text: Cache state and descriptive metadata are separate objects.
Store the four words at 88..100 and retain the cache base at sp+112.

steps.title: Clear the encoder cache for this invocation

quiz.prompt: What can an uncleared matching cache word cause?

choices.text: An INDEX that reconstructs the wrong pixel.
Automatic initialization in every external decoder.

hints.text: The decoder starts with a zero cache for every image.
Clear 256 bytes using a separate loop pointer; preserve t4..t7 for the header construction.

steps.title: Serialize the fixed header in file order

quiz.prompt: How are dimension bytes ordered in the output?

hints.text: The metadata’s in-memory layout is not the file header’s layout.
Emit four positioned bytes per dimension and only one byte per validated descriptive flag.

steps.title: Initialize a predictor and an empty pending run

quiz.prompt: Why can this image start with RUN?

choices.text: The header supplied black as a color sample.
Its first pixel equals the prescribed initial predictor.
Every image starts by repeating an uninitialized cache entry.

hints.text: The initial previous pixel is part of the format.
Set alpha 255 with RGB zero and retain a separate pending count; do not infer the predictor from the cache.

steps.title: Load one complete input word

quiz.prompt: What does the reduced remaining count exclude?

choices.text: The pixel already loaded into t0.
Only pixels that have explicit RGBA chunks.

hints.text: Loading a pixel and emitting its representation are separate events.
Use a four-byte word load, full-width pointer increment and one-pixel count decrement.

steps.title: Read a cache candidate without replacing it yet

quiz.prompt: Why must the old cache word be read before replacement?

choices.text: It is the next input pixel.
It determines whether INDEX is valid.

hints.text: Hash equality is weaker than complete pixel equality.
Retain the entry address and its previous word so the later comparison can inspect all four components.

steps.title: Separate repetition from a new-color decision

quiz.prompt: Which comparison identifies a repetition?

choices.text: Current pixel equals the header’s channels field.

hints.text: A run repeats the predictor, independently of whether a cache entry matches.
Handle equality first; on a different pixel, flush pending repetitions before the lookup path.

steps.title: Accumulate a run until a flush is required

quiz.prompt: When must a pending run be emitted?

choices.text: At length sixty-two or the final pixel.
Only when the entire input is black.

hints.text: The format limits one run chunk to sixty-two pixels.
Check both the pending count and the already reduced remaining-pixel count.

steps.title: Flush the biased run field

quiz.prompt: Which byte encodes one repetition?

hints.text: The stored field is one less than the repetition count.
Combine the biased low six bits with 192, store a byte and reset s5 only after writing it.

steps.title: Commit one encoder pixel’s state

quiz.prompt: Why update cache state for a repeated pixel?

choices.text: It changes the repeat count’s bias.
A later index can depend on that value.
It adds a mandatory extra command byte.

hints.text: The emitted stream and the encoder’s cache must describe the same history.
Store t0 through the retained t8 entry pointer, update s3 and inspect s1 before looping.

steps.title: Finish a working uniform-image subset

quiz.prompt: Which length belongs in the successful return?

hints.text: A successful subset can exercise framing before every command path exists.
Append exactly eight marker bytes, subtract the original destination pointer and write no extra terminator.

steps.title: Check complete cache equality and alpha

quiz.prompt: What must match to justify INDEX?

choices.text: Only RGB while alpha is retained separately.

hints.text: A cache collision is not a complete color match.
Compare t0 with the old word in t9; on a miss, inspect the current-versus-previous high byte before using RGB differences.

steps.title: Form signed representatives of byte differences

quiz.prompt: Why is minus one useful for zero-to 255 red?

choices.text: It describes the same modulo 256 change in a smaller field.
It instructs the decoder to clamp red.

hints.text: QOI additions wrap independently within each channel.
Normalize each difference modulo 256 into a signed-byte range before testing DIFF or LUMA.

steps.title: Emit a fitting DIFF command

quiz.prompt: What happens to a change of plus two?

choices.text: It fails the DIFF range test.
It is always clamped to plus one.

hints.text: A field must be proven representable before masking or placement.
Test each change plus two as unsigned less-than four; then place the three two-bit fields.

steps.title: Emit a verified cache index

quiz.prompt: How do entry byte offsets become slot numbers?

choices.text: Multiply the absolute address by four.
Keep the low six address bits directly.
Divide the offset from cache base by four.

hints.text: Each cache entry is one four-byte word.
Subtract s4 from t8, shift the difference right by two and emit only the resulting slot number.

steps.title: Emit green and two fitting residuals

quiz.prompt: What ranges must the residuals satisfy?

hints.text: Green and residual fields have different widths.
Subtract dG from dR and dB, test the biased residuals below sixteen and emit exactly two bytes on success.

steps.title: Use RGB when differences cannot represent the color

quiz.prompt: Why is no alpha byte needed for this literal?

choices.text: Alpha is unchanged from the predictor.
The input has no stored alpha.

hints.text: This path is selected only after alpha equality and failed difference ranges.
Write the full fe tag and three component bytes in file order, advancing by four.

steps.title: Emit explicit alpha with RGBA

quiz.prompt: Which byte order follows ff?

hints.text: The file’s RGBA order differs from the little-endian color word’s memory order.
Extract the fields from t0 in shifts 16,8,0,24 and emit four bytes after the full tag.

steps.title: Verify an equivalent stream independently

quiz.prompt: Which comparison is the completed encoder’s primary content check?

choices.text: Identical bytes to the worked file.

hints.text: A smaller file can still contain wrong colors, and a different file can still be correct.
Decode the exact returned bytes with an independent implementation and compare every component and header flag.

steps.title: Bound a file buffer before opening its path

quiz.prompt: Which capacity is valid for the loader?

choices.text: Thirty-eight bytes for this thirty-eight-byte file.
Zero bytes because EOF can be probed privately.

hints.text: The private EOF probe does not enlarge the caller’s declared buffer.
Reject zero and unsigned values above 20502 before the supplied load frame.

steps.title: Open input and retain the actual descriptor

quiz.prompt: Which descriptor should the next read use?

hints.text: A descriptor identifies this successful open, not a syscall number.
Preserve the returned handle in s3; the supplied cleanup marker starts at minus one.

steps.title: Accumulate only bytes actually read

quiz.prompt: What does a positive short read mean?

choices.text: Some bytes were accepted and another read is needed.

hints.text: Request size and returned count are different values.
Use buffer+accepted and capacity-accepted as the request, then add only the positive result to s4.

steps.title: Probe EOF outside an exactly full caller buffer

quiz.prompt: Where should the extra probe byte go?

choices.text: Private storage outside the caller buffer.

hints.text: A full buffer does not distinguish exact EOF from excess input.
Use sp+96 for the one-byte request and retain the caller’s accepted count unchanged.

steps.title: Close before validating loaded bytes

quiz.prompt: Why replace the validator’s successful count?

choices.text: The open call returned an unreliable descriptor.
The decoder has already produced the framebuffer.
The loader returns bytes, while validation returns pixels.

hints.text: Nested interfaces can use the same return register for different units.
Close first, call validation with s4 accepted bytes and return s4 after a zero status.

steps.title: Reject an impossible selected save count

quiz.prompt: Which value defines the bytes selected for saving?

choices.text: The previous input file’s length automatically.

hints.text: A pointer alone has no file-length information.
Check both count bounds before the supplied frame or any path access.

steps.title: Validate before truncating an existing file

quiz.prompt: Which event must precede truncate-mode open?

hints.text: Opening in write mode can destroy the old file immediately.
Use sp+80 for metadata and retain the supplied nonzero-status guard before the open body.

steps.title: Open output and observe truncation separately

quiz.prompt: What has successful truncate-mode open already changed?

hints.text: File lifecycle and byte-transfer completion are distinct boundaries.
Retain the returned s3 descriptor and initialize s4 without assuming any bytes have been written.

steps.title: Advance writes by the accepted count

quiz.prompt: Which count advances the source pointer?

hints.text: A short write has made progress but has not completed the request.
Pass bytes+accepted and selected-accepted, then add only the returned positive value.

steps.title: Close and return the full saved length

quiz.prompt: Why can this save return thirty-eight rather than thirty-five?

choices.text: Its input is the original serialized fixture.

hints.text: The saver’s job is validated transport, not representation selection.
Return the retained selected count after closing and use the supplied frame restore.

steps.title: Connect loading, reconstruction, encoding and saving

quiz.prompt: Which length should the caller pass from encoder to saver?

choices.text: The encoder’s complete returned byte count.

hints.text: The input file and encoded result need not have equal lengths.
At save_call compare a2 with the encoder result, then verify the saved file independently before the caller publishes status.

steps.title: Reuse the pipeline for the earlier sprite

quiz.prompt: What supplies an independent expected sprite image?

choices.text: The candidate encoder’s own output alone.

hints.text: A recognizable picture is useful but does not prove every byte or alpha value.
Expand the original rows from bit seven to bit zero and compare all sixty-four RGBA words.
